To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the activity of acetyl-choline-sterase increased in the striatum, cerebellum and the midbrain during development; (2) the percentage of acetylcholine-sterase that was extractable by sucrose solution from striatum decreased during maturation; and (3) the membrane bound fraction of the enzyme from the striatum was mostly composed of 10 S form, while the soluble fraction was mostly composed of a 4 S form.
The activity of acetycholinesterase (AChE) increased considerably during development of the rat striatum, but not in the cerebellar and the midbrain.
the membrane-bound form of acetyl-choline esterase in the developing striatum is much more labile than that in the adult striatum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular forms of acetylcholines-terase in the developing rat brain.
the developmental changes in acetyl-cholinestrase activity in different regions of the rat CNS and with the molecular forms of the enzyme in the developing and mature rat brain.
the developmental aspects of acetylcholine-esterase activity in the rat brain and the molecular forms of this enzyme in the striatum, a major target site for dopaminergic innervation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 4 S acetylcholin-esterase is more abundant in the soluble fraction than in the particulate fraction of the developing rat brain, while the reverse is true for the adult brain.
the 4 S acetyl-cholin-esterase form is predominant in the soluble fraction of developing brain while in adult brain the 10 S acetylcholin-esterase is predominant.
the 4 S acetylcholinesterease was a major form of the enzyme in the developing striatum and that it was converted into the 10 S enzyme during maturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activity of acetyl-cholineinesterase in rat striatum increased greatly during maturation.
the 4 S and 10 S forms of acetylcholine-terase are present in all the brain tissues examined, but the proportion of these two forms varies considerably with the age of the brain.

in the striatum of the developing rat, there is a greater amount of 4 S acetylcholinestrase in the membrane bound fraction and a smaller proportion in the isotonic soluble fraction than in the adult striatum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of the striatum involves a shift from a 4 S form to a 10 S form.

there are differences in acetylcholin-esterase forms and activities in various brain regions during development and in the adult brain, and that these differences are due to differences in the distribution of the molecular forms of the enzyme.

the development of the striatum is associated with a significant increase in the proportion of the soluble form of acetyl- cholinesterase, which is accompanied by a decrease in the proportion of membrane-bound enzyme.
